The Occupant of Room 412

Elena preferred the quiet of the West Wing, where the air tasted of floor wax and stale lilies. This story is a work of fiction.

Room 412 had been a storage closet for a decade, yet tonight the call button pulsed a steady, rhythmic amber.

The bed is still warm, she whispered to the empty corridor, a habit born of years spent tending to the dying.

She unlocked the door, expecting a short circuit, but found the thin mattress perfectly indented by a lingering weight.

Elena smoothed the sheets, her fingers trembling as she felt a pulse of genuine, human heat beneath the linen.

The bed is still warm.

She saw her own name on the whiteboard under a discharge date from November 2026 and realized the mirror held no reflection.

Elena wasn't the nurse on duty; she was the patient who simply refused to clock out.
